extracted.intended_audience: researchers and grant applicants preparing academic research grant proposals (e.g., R01 and equivalent)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing competitive academic research grant proposals, highlighting common reasons applications are not funded and areas to improve (significance, approach, team, budget, presentation, and process).

rubrics_metrics.name: The proposed research is incremental, not significant
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research is incremental, not significant
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers look for work that advances the field meaningfully. Applications that appear to make only small, incremental advances are less competitive. Emphasize novelty and clear impact; explain how the project moves the field forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: The hypothesis is not well-supported or compelling
rubrics_metrics.description: The hypothesis is not well-supported or compelling
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong proposal presents a clearly articulated, plausible, and important hypothesis. Provide logical rationale, prior data, and literature context to make the hypothesis compelling to reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: The 'so what?' question is not answered
rubrics_metrics.description: The "so what?" question is not answered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state significance and implications: why the work matters, who benefits, and how results will change knowledge, practice, or policy. Failing to justify importance reduces enthusiasm.

rubrics_metrics.name: The work is not state-of-the-art
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate awareness of current methods, findings, and technologies; explain how your approach uses or improves on the latest advances. Using outdated literature or methods undermines perceived relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewers express low overall enthusiasm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall enthusiasm affects funding decisions even if individual scores are mixed. Craft a clear, persuasive narrative and address likely reviewer concerns to generate positive reviewer engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insufficient preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data demonstrate feasibility and support key assumptions. Provide adequate pilot results, feasibility metrics, or prior work to convince reviewers the project is doable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed experiments will not prove the hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed experiments will not prove the hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure specific aims and experiments are logically linked to testing hypotheses. Design experiments with clear endpoints and controls so reviewers can see how results will address the central question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of experimental detail in the research strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of experimental detail in the research strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient methodological detail for reviewers to assess rigor and feasibility (experimental design, assays, models, controls). Avoid vague or high-level descriptions that leave critical steps unspecified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods are outdated
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contemporary, accepted methods and justify any choice of older techniques. Explain why your methods are appropriate and, if necessary, how you'll incorporate newer approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: No clear plan for rigorous, reproducible research
rubrics_metrics.description: No clear plan for rigorous, reproducible research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for rigor and reproducibility: blinding, randomization, replication, data management, analytic transparency, and validation. Lack of such plans reduces confidence in results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size justification is weak
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide power calculations or other justifications for sample sizes tied to expected effect sizes and statistical plans. Vague or absent justification raises concerns about validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis plan is inadequate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe statistical methods, models, handling of missing data, and multiple comparisons. Include who will perform analyses and any consulting/statistician support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unprovable hypothesis (a "fatal flaw")
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A hypothesis that cannot be tested or lacks feasible approaches is a fatal flaw; reviewers may stop discussing the application once they find such a flaw. Ensure hypotheses are testable and paired with appropriate experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unrealistic timeline
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a realistic project timeline and milestones aligned with scope and budget. Overly compressed schedules or mismatched timelines undermine feasibility judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overly ambitious scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose a scope that matches the funding level and time available. Avoid attempting too many aims or objectives; prioritize and phase work to show likely completion and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI lacks expertise in proposed methods
rubrics_metrics.description: PI lacks expertise in proposed methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the PI's qualifications and experience for the project. If gaps exist, propose collaborators, training, or mentors to cover methodological needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No clear plan for required collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: No clear plan for required collaborations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project depends on collaborators, include letters of support, defined roles, and plans for coordination. Vague or absent collaboration plans raise feasibility concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor/sponsor inadequately committed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For trainee- or early-career-focused proposals, present strong mentor(s) with clear commitments and documented support. Weak or generic mentor statements weaken the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record does not support the proposed work
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record does not support the proposed work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show prior productivity and relevant experience (publications, preliminary studies, prior funding). Ensure the team's history aligns with the proposed aims to build reviewer confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget does not align with proposed scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget does not align with proposed scope
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a budget that is realistic and clearly connected to specific aims and activities. Over- or under-budgeting relative to scope signals poor planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources at institution insufficient
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional resources (facilities, equipment, core services) needed to complete the project. If resources are lacking, propose solutions or appropriate external collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: No protected time for the PI
rubrics_metrics.description: No protected time for the PI
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the PI's committed effort (percentage effort/protected time) and institutional support to ensure the project leader can carry out the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poor organization, hard to follow
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write a well-structured, logically organized proposal with clear aims, transitions, and signposting. Disorganized narrative makes it hard for reviewers to assess the science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive jargon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, accessible language and define specialized terms. Excessive jargon can alienate or confuse reviewers, especially those outside narrow subfields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims page is unclear or hedging
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific Aims page is unclear or hedging
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft a concise, bold Specific Aims page that clearly states objectives, hypotheses, and impact. Avoid hedging language and make the central goals immediately understandable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures are illegible or uninformative
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear, well-labeled figures that convey key data, concepts, or experimental design. Poor-quality visuals reduce the proposal's clarity and persuasive power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inconsistencies between sections
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency (aims, methods, budget, timelines) across all sections. Conflicting information undermines credibility and suggests poor coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failed to contact the program officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Failed to contact the program officer
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage program officers early to confirm fit, funding mechanisms, and study section alignment. Not consulting them can lead to misaligned submissions or missed strategic advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wrong study section/funding mechanism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select an appropriate review panel and funding mechanism that match the proposal's topic, scope, and aims. Mis-targeted submissions may be reviewed by less-expert panels or judged against the wrong criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did not respond thoroughly to reviewer comments on resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: Did not respond thoroughly to reviewer comments on resubmission
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When resubmitting, address reviewer concerns point-by-point with substantive revisions and evidence. Superficial or incomplete responses reduce the chance of funding on resubmission.
